question.text: The amplitude of upper and lower side bands of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi><mi>M</mi></math> wave where a carrier signal with frequency <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>11</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>21</mn><mo> </mo><mi>MHz</mi><mo>,</mo></math> peak voltage <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>15</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> is amplitude modulated by a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>7</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>7</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kHz</mi></math> sine wave of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> amplitude are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>a</mi><mn>10</mn></mfrac><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>b</mi><mn>10</mn></mfrac><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> respectively. Then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi></mfrac></math> is_____.

solution.text:
In radio communications, a sideband is a band of frequencies higher than or lower than the carrier frequency, that are the result of the modulation process. The signal components above the carrier frequency constitute the upper sideband (USB), and those below the carrier frequency constitute the lower sideband (LSB).
